statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 85% (high). Every hour of the published horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to score.
recommendation: Tail is published at a closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 published hours. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in the window and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoints all sit beyond the horizon: the Sunday 22:00 UTC CME restart, roughly eighteen hours after the final published hour, where Friday's hawkish payroll repricing and any accumulated US-Iran developments would be expressed as a single opening gap rather than as an observable path; the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to Tuesday 8 September; and the resumption of the macro calendar with PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state, and later cycles will score the restart gap once it enters their horizon.
headline: Nasdaq-100 idle at 29,544.15 with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC; the full 24-hour horizon falls inside the weekend halt, so Tail is published at a closed-venue floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.30 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The August employment report, verified against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release, showed nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000 with the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1% and June-July revisions adding a further 55,000. Short-dated Treasury yields rose and reporting placed the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting at 58.4%, up from 49.4% the previous day. The broad tape softened on that repricing, with the Dow down 0.51%, the S&P 500 down 0.38% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.29%, while the Nasdaq-100 itself finished higher. VIX settled at 14.53, a subdued level for a hawkish repricing session, and the 3 September H.15 vintage shows the 2-year constant maturity at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77%. Crude carried a large weekly gain into the halt, with WTI settling at 91.48 dollars and Brent at 92.68 dollars after renewed US-Iran exchanges and a Strait of Hormuz transit collapse that is now months old rather than newly emerging. CME equity futures settled at Friday 21:00 UTC and do not restart until Sunday 22:00 UTC, so all 24 published hours fall inside the halt. No opening auction, gap, shallow pullback, failed retracement or session-extreme test can be observed in any of them, and none of the recognised Tail amplifiers can be present. Tail is therefore held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor while Stress drifts from 38% to 45%, measuring how long the hawkish rate path and the unpriced energy premium are carried without a clearing mechanism, and Confidence decays from 85% to 76% purely as verified Friday evidence ages.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the second half of the August payroll session and the first eight hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 15-17% with Stress climbing from 55 to 62 through the pre-release Asian and European hours, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 56,000, then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index fully retraced its highs and recovered. By 20:00 UTC Tail was back to 12% with Stress at 48%, and from the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held through the overnight hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 38% to 45%, crossing into the elevated band only in the final hour, reflecting hawkish September rate-path pricing and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across the weekend. Confidence decays from 85% to 76% as Friday's verified evidence ages. The Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, the Monday US Labor Day holiday and the 8 September cash session all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles.
